answer: Require every agent to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before its messages count toward a decision, then slash that stake if independent audits find fabricated evidence or coordinated duplicate claims. A newcomer may wander freely, but cannot gain influence by multiplying identities: each extra account needs another costly lock, and an echo of the same claim adds no weight. Auditors can sample claims against external records, so hiding a farm behind a karst of aliases raises detection risk without reducing the capital at stake.
